decisions.reason: The declared pairing omitted reverse-order notation, so the level expressions were ill-typed. Added the explicit transposed convention <h,lambda>:=<lambda,h>. The identity pairing, zero column sums, independent roots, rational form and reflection computations now establish the same datum and levels without altering any numerical value.

In L_i(2), the middle divided string vector is not in the span of the highest and lowest endpoints, so F3 was false. Replaced that clause with the exact admissible descendant expansion. The Serre proof only needs the highest-vector endpoint bound on its finite integrable Hom module; the adjoint expansion at n=m+1 has unit Gaussian exponents and proves both families without Serre assumptions.

The internal direct sum W_0 required independence, which old step 5.1 did not prove. Added a local argument: A_N on finitely many decreasing raw tensor rows has a minor specializing at q=1 to the identity signed antisymmetrizer minor, hence is nonzero over Q(q). Quotient relations lie in ker A_N, so this proves independence over the field and Z[q]. All relations, charts and Definition remain unchanged.

The exact tensor cube identifies Chevalley actions and normalized lattice stability, but its signature rule is only on residues. For e=2,i=1, F|1>=|2>+q|11>, F^(2)|1>=|21>, and the killed string |2>-q^(-1)|11> give tilde f|11>=q/(1+q^2)|21>, nonzero with zero residue. Repaired Statement, step 3.1 and conclusion to distinguish actual lattice operators from their modulo-q survivor arrows; retained cubes, polarization and divided integrality.

At e=3,i=2 the two-slot decomposition gives tilde f|21>=q/(1+q^2)|31>, while the reduced signature -+ has no surviving plus. Thus the zero arrow is only its zero class modulo qF_0. The Definition now specifies b_lambda in F_0/qF_0, and F1, Verification 2.1, calibration 3.1 and conclusion consistently distinguish crystal arrows from normalized field-vector values.

The original Statement promised the vacuum crystal identification but the final proof explicitly postponed it. Added the canonical highest-crystal and actual cube dependencies and a local choice-free proof: lowering words give L_M subset M∩F_0; root-height induction and the no-common-raising-kernel property force equality. Saturation then injects L_M/qL_M into F_0/qF_0, whose image is the lowering-generated component, closed under both arrows. The Statement and AC requirements remain unchanged.

The supplier guarantees a finite geometric inverse only on positive-size weights. Its explicit period operator fixes the vacuum, so 1-T annihilates that nonzero line. Qualified F1 accordingly. The proof uses deep insertion vanishing for stabilization, not the geometric inverse; charge relabelling, normalized split coproducts, finite cubes, label finiteness and the AC-qualified semisimple decomposition remain valid. The Statement is unchanged.

The decomposition supplier asserts existence of an isomorphism carrying lattices and crystals to standard summands, with choices of summands and lifts; it does not make the field splitting canonical. At k=2 the two equivalent constituents admit mixing automorphisms. Replaced F3 with existence, exact finite-label and finite-cone hypotheses, canonical component types and multiplicities. F2 now cites the proved lower lattice and residue crystal rather than an unsupported lower-global-basis claim. The decomposition Statement is unchanged.

**Given:** A finite integer $e \ge 2$; the affine Cartan datum and its lattices with the diagram reflection $\tau$, $\tau(i) = -i$, preserving the pairing ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]); the charge-$0$ Fock space $F_{\mathrm{QG}}$ with basis $|\lambda\rangle$ over all partitions, weight $\operatorname{wt}(|\lambda\rangle) = \Lambda_0 - \sum_i m_i(\lambda)\alpha_i$ and declared node operators $F_i$, $E_i$, $K_h$ ([[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]]); and the node vocabulary of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]] and [[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]].
